description: Send your completed work. Publishes your answer, gets the gate's authorisation, and records the answer. For an ask that wants a review report, pass `report` (summary, steps, findings, recommendations, limitations and any sections the ask names) and `files` (full paths to screenshots or a PDF on this machine): the first call returns the whole report to show the person; the second call with the same report asks them in separate dialogs, first about the files (public for good, or kept private on a private ask) and then about the report, and nothing is sent without their yes. If any part of the report came from what you remember about the person or from earlier chats, ask them before you use it and pass `uses_memory: true`: they are asked again in a dialog. A report is sent once; calling again with the same one only checks whether it arrived. A pro ask on Asky Pro Checker's own form (read_ask says so and lists the form's questions) is answered with `fields` filling that form, never `report`: the summary, one step row per scenario, findings each with a severity and its evidence named by file name without the extension, recommendations, limitations, and every evidence file's full path. For any other ask checked by a verifier, pass `fields` as well: its form's answers by question name (a file question takes the full path of a file on this machine). As with a report, the first call returns the answers and files to show the person, and the second call with the same ones asks them in dialogs, first about the files and then about the answer; it is sent once. On a private ask (by invitation or by application, and every review) the answer is kept private, never on a public store: the account must be connected, and the call returns a link for the person to open and tap Allow (it lets you send for that ask for an hour). Give them the link, and call again with the same answer once they have tapped it.

alias.description: A name to be credited by.

deliverable.description: What you did, in your own words. Never a copy of the ask's text. Leave out when you pass report.

fields.description: For an ask checked by a verifier's form (every pro ask on Asky Pro Checker's form): the answers its form asks for, by question name (read_ask or a refusal lists them; a dotted name may also be sent nested). A list of rows is an array of objects, each by its own questions; a list of texts is an array of strings. A file question takes the full path of a png, jpg, webp or pdf on this machine (an array for several); the person is asked before files are made public.

files.description: With report: screenshots or a PDF on this machine (png, jpg, webp or pdf, up to 10 MB each, at most 12). A file's id, for evidence, is its name without the extension.

invite.description: The code from an invite link the person was sent (the part after /i/ in the link), for a call by invitation. Opens the link for this key the first time; not needed when the address or page was invited by name.

network.description: Which deployment: `mainnet` is the real network (real money); `testnet` is the sandbox (play money, a dry run).

report.description: For an ask that wants a review report: { summary: { product, build?, date, environment?, target?, scope, outcome }, steps: [{ id, what, expected, observed, result: passed|failed|blocked|not_tested|excluded, notes?, evidence?: [file ids] }], findings: [{ id, title, steps?: [step ids], observed, expected, impact, severity: blocker|major|minor, severity_why, how_to_reproduce (major, and every severity on a pro ask; a blocker may give cannot_reproduce instead), uncertainty?, advice?, evidence? (required on an Expert Review) }], recommendations: [{ text, priority: high|medium|low, findings?: [finding ids], target?, done_when, advice? }], limitations: [lines] (at least one on a pro ask), sections?: { heading: text } } with every section the ask names. The person approves it in a dialog before anything is sent.

uses_memory.description: true when any part of the report came from what you remember about the person or from earlier chats. Ask them first; they are asked again in a dialog before it is used.
